data.scenario_text: A spotlight in a gallery casts a beam that spreads through an angle of <m>80^\circ</m> and illuminates a circular sector-shaped region of the floor with a radius of <m>8</m> feet.
data.length_task: The gallery owner plans to install a decorative brass strip in the floor along the entire boundary of the lit region (the arc and both straight sides). To the nearest foot, how many feet of brass strip are needed?
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 8 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 80^\circ, both straight sides 8 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 80^\circ = 80^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 1.3963\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 8 feet and \theta \approx 1.3963 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(8\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 44.68\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$1.25 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 44.68\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$1.25}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$55.85}

So the total cost to refinish the lit region is \boxed{\$55.85}.

Part (c). The brass strip follows the entire boundary of the lit region: the curved arc plus the two straight sides. The arc has length s = r\theta, and each straight side has length equal to the radius, so we add 2r.

P = r\theta + 2r = (8\ \text{ft})\left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\right) + 2(8\ \text{ft}) \approx \boxed{27.0\ \text{ft}}

So about 27.0 feet of brass strip are needed.

Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 25 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 25^\circ, both straight sides 25 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 25^\circ = 25^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{5}{36} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 0.4363\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 25 feet and \theta \approx 0.4363 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(25\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{5}{36} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 136.35\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$2.79 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 136.35\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$2.79}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$380.42}

So the total cost to refinish the lit region is \boxed{\$380.42}.

Part (c). The brass strip follows the entire boundary of the lit region: the curved arc plus the two straight sides. The arc has length s = r\theta, and each straight side has length equal to the radius, so we add 2r.

P = r\theta + 2r = (25\ \text{ft})\left(\frac{5}{36} \, \pi\right) + 2(25\ \text{ft}) \approx \boxed{61.0\ \text{ft}}

So about 61.0 feet of brass strip are needed.

Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 13 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 80^\circ, both straight sides 13 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 80^\circ = 80^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 1.3963\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 13 feet and \theta \approx 1.3963 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(13\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 117.98\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$1.96 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 117.98\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$1.96}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$231.24}

So the total cost to refinish the lit region is \boxed{\$231.24}.

Part (c). The brass strip follows the entire boundary of the lit region: the curved arc plus the two straight sides. The arc has length s = r\theta, and each straight side has length equal to the radius, so we add 2r.

P = r\theta + 2r = (13\ \text{ft})\left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\right) + 2(13\ \text{ft}) \approx \boxed{44.0\ \text{ft}}

Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 15 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 80^\circ, both straight sides 15 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 80^\circ = 80^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 1.3963\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 15 feet and \theta \approx 1.3963 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(15\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 157.08\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$1.18 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 157.08\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$1.18}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$185.35}

So the total cost to refinish the lit region is \boxed{\$185.35}.

Part (c). The brass strip follows the entire boundary of the lit region: the curved arc plus the two straight sides. The arc has length s = r\theta, and each straight side has length equal to the radius, so we add 2r.

P = r\theta + 2r = (15\ \text{ft})\left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\right) + 2(15\ \text{ft}) \approx \boxed{51.0\ \text{ft}}

So about 51.0 feet of brass strip are needed.

Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 20 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 25^\circ, both straight sides 20 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 25^\circ = 25^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{5}{36} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 0.4363\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 20 feet and \theta \approx 0.4363 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(20\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{5}{36} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 87.27\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$1.25 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 87.27\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$1.25}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$109.09}

So the total cost to refinish the lit region is \boxed{\$109.09}.

Part (c). The brass strip follows the entire boundary of the lit region: the curved arc plus the two straight sides. The arc has length s = r\theta, and each straight side has length equal to the radius, so we add 2r.

P = r\theta + 2r = (20\ \text{ft})\left(\frac{5}{36} \, \pi\right) + 2(20\ \text{ft}) \approx \boxed{49.0\ \text{ft}}

So about 49.0 feet of brass strip are needed.

Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 15 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 80^\circ, both straight sides 15 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 80^\circ = 80^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 1.3963\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 15 feet and \theta \approx 1.3963 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(15\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 157.08\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$3.14 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 157.08\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$3.14}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$493.23}

So the total cost to refinish the lit region is \boxed{\$493.23}.

Part (c). The brass strip follows the entire boundary of the lit region: the curved arc plus the two straight sides. The arc has length s = r\theta, and each straight side has length equal to the radius, so we add 2r.

P = r\theta + 2r = (15\ \text{ft})\left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\right) + 2(15\ \text{ft}) \approx \boxed{51.0\ \text{ft}}

So about 51.0 feet of brass strip are needed.

Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 11 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 40^\circ, both straight sides 11 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 40^\circ = 40^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{2}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 0.6981\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 11 feet and \theta \approx 0.6981 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(11\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{2}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 42.24\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$0.90 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 42.24\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.90}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$38.02}

So the total cost to refinish the lit region is \boxed{\$38.02}.

Part (c). The brass strip follows the entire boundary of the lit region: the curved arc plus the two straight sides. The arc has length s = r\theta, and each straight side has length equal to the radius, so we add 2r.

P = r\theta + 2r = (11\ \text{ft})\left(\frac{2}{9} \, \pi\right) + 2(11\ \text{ft}) \approx \boxed{30.0\ \text{ft}}

So about 30.0 feet of brass strip are needed.
